editorial:
Ever feel like you are talking to someone but they just do not get it? You will find that feeling turned into a weird, wild ride in this collection of three short stories. It is not a normal movie with a straight plot; instead, it uses stop-motion puppets and strange objects to show how people fail to understand each other. The vibe is a bit creepy and very funny at the same time, making you feel like you are inside a strange dream where nothing works the way it should. 

The way the objects move is really impressive and keeps you hooked even when things get bizarre. You will love the creativity, though some parts might feel too slow or too odd if you prefer a standard story. It is perfect for anyone who likes art that pushes boundaries. To get the best look at the detailed textures and puppet work, you should try to find the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection. If you are in a rush, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to experience these strange tales without committing too much time.
endingExplained: The final segments show that no matter how hard people try to talk, they end up trapped in their own bubbles. In the end, the characters stop trying to use words and instead become part of the machinery or objects around them. It wraps up by showing that communication is often broken beyond repair. Everything turns into a loop of noise and clutter, proving that talking does not always lead to understanding.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange animation and dark humor.
